title: node-ipc 10.1.1, 10.1.2 and the peacenotwar dependency
summary: The node-ipc maintainer published 10.1.1 and 10.1.2, which overwrote files on hosts that geolocated to Russia or Belarus, then moved a milder payload into a new dependency, peacenotwar, which reached the widely installed 9.x line through 9.2.2. This was protestware from the package's own author rather than a credential compromise, and the two payloads are different threat shapes; package and advisory timestamps come from the sources listed below, while the seven services, their descriptions and their lockfile resolution times are invented demo fixtures that name no real victim.

compromisedVersions.name: peacenotwar
compromisedVersions.note: Publish time and scripts read first hand from the peacenotwar packument, which is still published. It declares only test and prepare scripts, so there is no install hook: the desktop file is written when the module is imported. No GHSA names peacenotwar itself; it is listed here because it is the artifact that carried the payload into node-ipc 9.2.2 and 11.x.

compromisedVersions.name: node-ipc
compromisedVersions.note: Publish time from the node-ipc packument. This is the version that carried peacenotwar into the 9.x line that @vue/cli-shared-utils depended on, which is why the widely deployed blast radius is this payload and not the file overwriting code in 10.1.1 and 10.1.2. npm removed the version, so the absence of an install hook comes from the advisory rather than from its manifest.

advisories.summary: Embedded malicious code in node-ipc: 10.1.1 and 10.1.2 overwrote files with a heart symbol on hosts whose IP geolocated to Russia or Belarus. Tracked as CVE-2022-23812.

Hidden functionality in node-ipc: version 9.2.2 depends on peacenotwar, which writes a protest file to the desktop when imported. The advisory lists 9.2.2 as the only affected version and the 9.x line has no later release, so there is no fixed version to name.
node-ipc behaviour change: 11.0.0 through 11.1.0 depend on peacenotwar, and 12.0.0 removed the dependency.

services.name: desktop-build-agent
services.description: Build agent for the Vue frontends, which reaches node-ipc through the @vue/cli-shared-utils dependency on the 9.x line.

services.name: admin-web
services.description: Internal admin frontend on the Vue CLI 5 line, refreshed hours before disclosure.

services.name: dev-portal
services.description: Developer documentation portal, last locked in February and therefore on a clean 10.1.0.

services.name: internal-tools-web
services.description: Internal tools frontend refreshed the day after disclosure onto the version the advisory names as fixed.

services.name: release-runner
services.description: Release pipeline runner rebuilt after the Vue CLI patch, which moved the dependency to the maintained fork.
